questions.q: If the receipts side (debit) of a reconstructed cash book totals ₦100,000, and the total of known business payments plus the closing cash balance on the payments side (credit) amounts to only ₦80,000, what is the most logical accounting treatment for the missing ₦20,000 on the credit side?
options: It is treated as unrecorded cash sales
It is assumed to be unrecorded cash drawings or stolen cash
It is added to the opening capital
It is recorded as an increase in trade debtors
questions.explain: Incomplete records often feature balancing figures. If total documented cash receipts (₦100,000) exceed total known cash payments and cash still on hand (₦80,000), cash has gone missing. This ₦20,000 shortfall is usually assumed to be unrecorded **cash drawings** by the owner, or less frequently, defalcation/stolen cash.

questions.q: When preparing final accounts from a set of incomplete records, the **opening capital** balance is typically found by preparing which of the following statements?
options: A Trading Account for the previous year
A Statement of Affairs as at the beginning of the financial year
questions.explain: Because a proper trial balance wasn't extracted in a single entry system, the opening capital must be derived by preparing a **Statement of Affairs** (which acts like a balance sheet) as at the beginning of the year. $\text{Opening Assets} - \text{Opening Liabilities} = \text{Opening Capital}$.
